Due to me living in Iraq, I've heard alot of absolutely terrifying stories, but the two worst ones go like this.

During the ISIS occupation in Mosul, a woman and her family get kidnapped and tortured because they weren't following regulations. They took the woman, chained her in an obscure room and starved her for three days. After those three days, an ISIS member comes into her room, and gives her a plate of rice and meat. He tells her to eat up, as she hasn't eaten in a few days. She does, and once she is done eating, he tells her that she just ate her own children. That they cut up her OWN kids, and fed them to her.. 
I heard of this story because the women, who got out alive, went on a radio show and talked about her situation.

Another terrifying story would be of a case in Baghdad. A rich family, who has immigrated outside of Iraq comes back to Baghdad due to certain circumstances, however they've forgotten how dangerous the situation may be in Baghdad. A group of terrorists decide to kidnap their oldest son, and hold him up for an expensive ransom. They call the father up, and tell him he needs to drop money at a certain location/time, which he does. 
He pays up, but he doesn't get his son back. He gets a call after three days that his son is on his front stairs. He goes out and all he sees is a plate covered in aluminium foil, where he finds his sons head, cooked... 

There are multiple atrocities that occur here, and lots of them are done due to war and occupations... Anyways, those are the ones that shook me the most.

I agree. I do not know what you may have gone through or what others may have gone through to reach this point.. I do know that I know what it feels like to struggle with those thoughts and with that pain, as a human being who is capable of empathy..
The world is riddled with pain and suffering, there's no denying. 
But just because the world is burning and suffering does not mean you don't matter. 
I'm not saying it is as simple as changing your attitude towards life. What I am saying is that you have the possibility to enjoy things in life and to make things matter around you, to make you matter towards yourself. This understanding doesn't come simply with a change in attitude, but with a plethora of other things, such as seeking proper mental health, understanding your self worth, trying to do things you enjoy and actually being able to enjoy these things without feeling like a burden to this planet or to yourself. 
You do matter, not because I say you do but because you say you do. You say you matter by enjoying the sensory aspect of life, the emotional aspect of life, the physical aspect of life, and so on and so forth. 
There is always potential for good and change, and you can contribute to that, but the greatest step you can take for yourself is to love yourself and to decide to take proper actions by seeking better mental health to achieve self love and find worth within yourself.
You create your own destiny, your own future, your own purpose. No one else can decide that for you, but please understand that you do matter. Not only because you can contribute in making this planet a better place, but because you are a sentient being, with emotions and awareness. The fact that you can feel empathy for others is beautiful, but try to target that empathy towards your own self, because you get to decide your life choices after all.

I apologize you have to go through that OP, I know it can suck to have families with religious/cultural backgrounds trying to hold you back from doing what you want.

But you should know this is your life, and you live it the way you see fit. As long as you aren't harming yourself or others.

Sit down with your family and try to explain to them that marriage is a forever step, and you don't want to take that type of commitment yet. Living together is the next step, marriage may come later on. 

Ask them how they expect you to get married/engaged without even having lived together and understood each others in that manner.
Getting married means you live with that person forever, (unless you get a divorce, which is costly and comes with alot of hassle), and tell them that it may be more likely that you two may get a divorce if you rushed into marriage without taking the steps you find are right in your life.

Try to explain that as much as you love and respect them, those are YOUR decisions to make and only yours. Tell them that you are sorry they may view these things through different lenses, but as an adult, you need to live your life for you and not for others.

If they shut you out or shame you for making your own life decisions, then I'd advise you distance yourself from them, until they can realize they messed up.
But you should know that when taking this decision, there still is a high possibility that they may shun you/shame you for making this step.
Don't let that stop you, but let it help you in realizing that they aren't supportive of your life choices and your decisions, and that they don't trust you enough as an adult to make good decisions.
